plain: A serious plea or protest against someone's action.

webster.text: Reasoning with a person in opposition to his conduct; the act of pressing on a person reasons or arguments against the impropriety of his conduct, and in some cases, demanding redress or urging reformation.

example.quote: Jersey herself; by which she expressly refused to comply with a constitutional requisition of Congs. and yielded no farther to the expostulations of their deputies, than barely to rescind her vote of refusal without passing any positive act of compliance.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, June 19, 1787
